rationale.text: The official text does not say what makes a document type valid. The glossary defines a document type only as the reference data that tells user agents the technical characteristics of the page's languages, and the methodology (shared with 8.1.1 and 8.1.3) only says to check that it is valid. Neither names a reference list: the HTML standard's doctype and its obsolete permitted forms, the W3C list of recommended declarations, or the published DTDs. A check that faults a doctype outside a list would rest on an interpretation the text does not give, so no failure is claimed. A pass cannot be proven from the rendered page either. The DOM keeps only a doctype's name and its public and system identifiers, and reports a missing identifier and an empty one the same way: <!DOCTYPE html> and <!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC ""> (a parse error under the HTML standard) look identical. It also does not show a second declaration placed later in the source, which the parser drops. Even the one DOM-visible case that is invalid under any reading, a declaration with no name (<!DOCTYPE>), is too rare to justify a check and could in principle be added by a script. What would raise it: an official reference for "valide", and access to the source as served, which spec section 15 and decision Q9 leave out of v1. Applicability is judgment: the wording says "Pour chaque page web", and whether a page with no doctype makes this test not applicable or failed is not settled by the text; moreover the DOM cannot show whether a page holds a misplaced declaration. Needs is empty.
